<!-- pr-reviewer: 53e4aebbf42b5e80654a46bf6442ae4181a3e0e1 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers; a few non-blocking notes below.

Reviewed at head 53e4aeb, trial-merged with `upstream/main` (already up to date, no conflicts). The diff touches no `build.rs`, `.github/`, `scripts/` or Cargo files. The only script change is the `fanuc-lathe.cps` header and tool-note text.

## What looks good
- **The core argument holds.** `nose_tip::control_point_path` adds one constant vector r*(ox,oz) to every point and arc centre of the nose-centre path. Because the insert is rigid, the nose centre then traces the cached CAM path exactly, including on tapers and arcs (the unit test builds the 30 degree taper as profile plus r*normal). The cache, verifier, stock sim and gouge laws are untouched; the diff only changes the stream handed to `post::dump` in `posting::op_streams`.
- **Numbers checked.**
  - A Ø19.05 OD finish posts X19.05 and a face posts Z0 (`an_od_finish_posts_the_finished_diameter_and_a_face_posts_z0`, app `lathe_nose_tip`).
  - Every orientation equals cache + r*offset (`every_orientation_moves_the_centre_by_its_own_tip`).
  - In X, the shift is r on the radius, so 2r on a diameter word. The facing golden moves X by -1.6 (2*0.8) and Z by -0.8 for r 0.8, and the profile golden by the same amounts.
- **Defaults and refusals.**
  - A tool without a stated orientation takes 2 (turning) or 3 (boring) through `Tool::lathe_orientation`. The project key is additive and skipped when unset.
  - Codes outside 1-9 are refused in `Tool::validate` (command creation and file read) and again at post in `checked_orientation`.
  - An orientation that cannot present the cut's contacts is refused by name, listing the fitting orientations. [1,5,6] is reproduced.
- **Goldens.** Only `facing.nc` and `profile_rough_finish.nc` changed. Every changed line is a pure shift of the amounts above, plus the new `ORIENTATION 2` tool-note text. No snapshot PNGs, no CHANGELOG edit, and a decision record is included.
- **The `lathe.mch` X band** is pinned both ways: facing to centre fits, and a real over-travel (X-10) still refuses by name. The decision file records why the old #493 rule is overturned.

## Local results (merged with main)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-post` (unit incl. nose_tip, comp, post_engine etc.), `camcraft-tools` | all pass |
| app: `lathe_nose_tip` 6, `lathe_post` 7, `lathe_post_refusals` 5, `lathe_post_g76` 5, `lathe_stroke` 7, `lathe_field_tools` 2, `lathe_field_sim` 6, `lathe_cross_drill` 5, `lathe_spindle_*` (fit, keyed, law) | pass |
| app: `conformance` 6, `posting` 17, `golden_cl` 23, `project_roundtrip` 70, `commands_undo` 32, `solid_law_goldens`, `mill2d_b`, `mill2d_c`, `operations` 117 (6 ignored) | pass |
| app: `machine`, `machine_edit`, `machine_library`, `tormach_machines`, all `tool_*` suites, all 14 `turning_*` suites | pass |
| motion: `drilling` unit tests, `center_cut_owed` | pass |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` | 377 passed, 1 failed (see below) |
| clippy app/post/motion/tools/ui `--all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

```
egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds: egui headless run failed: No suitable graphics adapter found
```
That is the review machine having no GPU adapter (the test needs a window). It is not caused by this PR. I also reverted the `lathe.mch` floor to 0 locally: `lathe_x_stays_a_centreline_band` and `a_facing_pass_to_centre_fits_the_built_in_lathe_x_band` both fail ("X -0.800 outside 0..320"), so the pins bite. The file was restored.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **The band change does not feed the in-app check.** `machine::check_document` (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs:179,256`) reads `cache.path`, the nose-centre path, so the posted control point at -r is never compared to the stroke. The new test does that comparison itself on `posted_path`. The widening is therefore a margin for when the check reads the posted path (the author's filed P1, stroke check on world X vs the Y meridian). The decision text ("the post writes the control point, so the floor was wrong") reads a little stronger than the code today. Fine to keep.
2. **PathPilot evidence versus the table.** The decision record cites a Hub 8L facing with orientation 3 ending past centre. In this PR's table, 3 is (+X,-Z) and the facing rule says facing fits only [2,6,7]. So PathPilot's number 3 facing past centre does not obviously match our numbering of 3 (it could be a rear versus front post convention, or the X-0.0174 is overshoot). The [1,5,6] listing independently corroborates 1, 5 and 6, but 2 and 3 rest on the LinuxCNC figure, whose text I could not confirm outside the figure. Worth a maintainer glance with real tooling before #626 builds on it.
3. **Signed radius.** The shift is applied in the world coordinate with the sign of `dr` (`nose_tip.rs:67-79`), which assumes the part's radius is on the + side of the meridian (as the lathe kernels produce). A path on the -X or -Y side would shift the wrong way. A guard or a test for that would be cheap if a mirrored setup is ever supported.
4. Grooving and parting blades (corner touch-off) and the stroke-check meridian issue are filed as follow-ups, as the PR says. Agreed they are not this PR's blockers. `posting.rs` is 1099 lines (already over; this PR adds about 10).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
